name: Fairbanks House

dates.altered: The 1930s HABS data sheet records 'practically no detrimental alterations except the removal of the original casement windows'; later lean-tos and wings are the node's own note.
dates.note: Three dates are on the record because three sources give them: the node's exemplar says 1637 (dendrochronology, late 1630s); the Wikipedia infobox says ca. 1641; the HABS data sheet says 'c.1656 et seq.'. None is edited to agree with another.

quotes.text: This is perhaps the earliest and most important house of the 17th century standing in Massachusetts. It has suffered from practically no detri- mental alterations except the removal of the original casement windows many of which, however, are preserved in the house. It retains many fine open timber ceilings, very rare moulded sheathing and weatherboarded wainscot.
